newsitem.title: USA: Delaware judge to rule later on Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Delaware judge to rule later on Great Western.

text.p: A Delaware judge said Friday he would rule later on a request by H.F. Ahmanson & Co. to delay a June 13 vote by Great Western Financial Corp. shareholders on a proposed merger with Washington Mutual Inc.

"I do plan to reserve (a) decision on this motion and will issue an opinion as soon as I can," Delaware Chancery Court Vice Chancellor Jack Jacobs said after hearing oral arguments by contestants in the thrift-industry takeover battle.

Attorneys for Ahmanson and a Great Western shareholders group argued that Great Western's board acted improperly and violated its own bylaws by delaying the company's annual meeting, at which Ahmanson is seeking to replace three of 11 board members, until a vote on the Washington mutual merger could also be held.

Great Western agreed to a proposed stock-swap merger with Washington Mutual on March 6, in an effort to thwart a hostile bid by Ahmanson, the Irwindale, Calif.-based parent of Home Savings of America.

Ahmanson's all-share bid, raised later in March, was worth about $48.90 per share, or $6.8 billion, at Friday's stock prices. That compares with about $50.07, or $6.97 billion, for the Washington Mutual bid.
Ahmanson attorney John Hardiman said holding the two votes June 13 would deprive Great Western shareholders of the opportunity to consider the merger before any new board members could be heard from.
"Shareholders who felt they wanted to change the mix of the people on the board at this critical juncture are not being permitted to do it," he said.
Ahmanson had earlier won a Great Western shareholder solicitation to hold the annual meeting May 6, but confirmation of the victory came too late to hold the meeting.

Ahmanson wants the merger vote to be held six weeks after the annual meeting, saying any new, independent board members should be able to consider the deal and have an opportunity to influence other Great Western board members.
Great Western attorney Rodman Ward said the Great Western board acted responsibly and within its legal authority. "I think they went forward ... in a diligent way," he said.
Any delay in the merger of the two firms could erode the value of the deal, Ward said. "The continued uncertainty at Great Western is damaging the asset," he said.
